nodes.description: Should we hire two more developers now, or keep the team as it is and subcontract overflow work?

unit_reading.source_quote: Our goal is to grow monthly revenue from about £110,000 today to at least £150,000 within 9 months

rows.brief_text: We run a 12-person software consultancy. Should we hire two more developers now, or keep the team as it is and subcontract overflow work? Our goal is to grow monthly revenue from about £110,000 today to at least £150,000 within 9 months. There is about a 30% chance that our largest client, who is 40% of our revenue, cuts their contract this year. Each new hire would cost about £5,500 a month, and subcontractors cost about £600 a day.

request.message: Add a risk: our largest client might cancel their contract, maybe 20 - 40% in the next 6 months. If they cancel, monthly revenue would drop.

rows.observed_assistant_text:
The model already includes revenue loss from a largest-client contract cut.

- Its probability is your earlier 30%; your new 20–40% range and six-month horizon are not represented.
- Adding cancellation separately could count the same revenue loss twice.

Do you mean to refine that existing risk, or add cancellation as a separate event from a contract reduction?
